The proposed Human Resources Leadership specialization within the B.A. in Business Studies is designed to prepare students to lead people and organizations in a rapidly evolving workplace.
Effective leadership today requires more than technical business knowledge; it demands an understanding of human behavior, organizational culture, social dynamics, and the systems that shape how people work together.
This specialization integrates these dimensions by combining business courses in management and leadership by using interdisciplinary coursework to deepen students’ understanding of interpersonal communication, group dynamics, diversity, equity and inclusion, and organizational systems.
Students pursuing this specialization will explore how organizations attract, develop, motivate, and retain talent, and how leaders foster environments where individuals and teams can thrive.
They will gain skills in areas such as leadership communication, conflict resolution, negotiation, and change management, while also examining the broader social and cultural factors that influence workplace relationships and organizational outcomes.

This interdisciplinary approach reflects the evolving expectations of employers, who increasingly seek graduates with the ability to manage people effectively, lead diverse teams, and navigate complex organizational challenges.
It also aligns with national trends in workforce development and talent management, where human resources leadership is emerging as a strategic driver of organizational success.
By leveraging existing courses across multiple disciplines that are not currently part of the B.A. in Business Studies curriculum, this specialization can be implemented efficiently while significantly expanding the career pathways available to graduates, including roles in human resources, talent acquisition, organizational development, employee relations, and leadership consulting.
Students completing the Human Resources specialization will be able to: Apply theories of motivation, leadership, and organizational behavior to real-world business challenges.
Design strategies for talent development, performance management, and workforce planning.
Lead with cultural intelligence and build inclusive environments that leverage diversity as a source of innovation.

Use insights from sociology and human development to address complex interpersonal and systemic issues in organizations.
Communicate effectively and resolve conflict in professional settings.
Aligned with the University of Rhode Island’s mission as the state’s flagship land- and sea-grant research institution, the Human Resources Leadership specialization advances URI’s commitment to student success, community engagement, and inclusive excellence.
This specialization prepares students to become ethical, adaptive leaders who strengthen Rhode Island’s workforce, support organizational resilience, and foster equitable and thriving workplaces in a rapidly changing global economy.
Through applied learning and interdisciplinary collaboration, students develop the capacity to lead with empathy, integrity, and strategic vision, which are qualities central to URI’s role in building informed residents and leaders who make a positive impact locally and globally.
